problems: Shared harness: measureBytesPerEntry in dsa/src/_shared/mem.ts (not mine, left untouched) takes its snapshots synchronously. V8 sweeps dead objects and frees ArrayBuffer backing stores concurrently, so the measured column can be too low or negative. A synchronous probe stayed off by up to about 160 B/entry however many gc() calls it made; an async probe that awaited 30 ms between three gc() calls matched allocated within 1%. Recommendation for the harness owner: make it async, or await a macrotask between gc() calls. My bench now pre-flattens its ConsString keys, which removed the largest negative bias, but some runs still record noisy measured values (for example path at 10^5 about -5 to -10 B/entry).

Property tests at nightly size (PLT_PROP_RUNS=10000) take about 22 s and exceed vitest's default 5 s testTimeout. The nightly job needs --testTimeout or a per-test timeout. All four seeds I tried pass.
`pnpm exec vitest bench --run --project dsa` fails ('No projects matched the filter'); the working command is `--project 'dsa (bench)'`.

Benchmark shape assertions are sensitive to CPU contention: 1 of 7 runs failed the p95 shape test (3.30x against a limit of 3) while about 25 agents ran in parallel (load average 12-19). All other runs gave 0.99-1.42x. Judge it on the lab runner.

Contract interpretation 1: R1 as written cannot hold for keys longer than 65,535 units, because lblLen is Uint16 and the spec says such labels are split. The implementation exempts exactly the unary nodes that cannot merge (lblLen[n] + lblLen[child] > 65,535). This is documented in the code, the README and the DSA.md template; it needs keys far beyond Plotinium's 4,133-unit maximum.
Contract interpretation 2: debugCorrupt('unary-node') skips the root, because clearing a unary root would not break R1. The TrieCorruption doc comment in index.ts was updated to say so.

test_changes: No test files changed; trie.test.ts and trie.prop.test.ts pass unmodified. One change in dsa/bench/trie.bench.ts, in the DSA-TRIE-03 memory test only: `for (const k of keys) k.charCodeAt(0);` runs before measureBytesPerEntry, with a comment. Reason: the corpus keys are template-literal V8 ConsStrings, and insert's first charCodeAt flattens each one. The freed cons cells were subtracted from the trie's heap growth, so measured bytes/entry for path and hist came out negative (-28 to -30 at 10^4 and 10^5). Flattening first makes the probe count only the trie. The assertions are unchanged, and the change can only make them stricter, since a negative measured value passed trivially before.
